title: predicatory-differentiation
description: A predicatory comparison that asks what evidence separates one valuation from another, realized as an evidence residual rather than a differential calculus; given v <=_k w it records the cellwise positive and negative evidence present in w but not already in v.

residual.description: the partial operation d_k(v,w) recording the cellwise positive and negative evidence in w not already in v; computed coordinatewise on a twist product via relative complement/residuum, and by finite lookup on FOUR

knowledge-comparable.description: the residual is well-typed only when v <=_k w in the knowledge order; for non-comparable inputs the residual question is replaced by the FOUR symmetric evidence difference

residual-not-differential.description: a residual calculus, not a differential-category structure: it assumes no additive symmetric monoidal structure, coalgebra modality, or differential combinator on the predication settling category
